subject: ela
cluster: Research to Build and Present Knowledge
intro: Twelfth graders gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the strengths and limitations of each source in terms of the task, purpose, and audience; integrate information selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and overreliance on any one source, and following a standard citation format.

items.prompt: What is the difference between QUOTING and PARAPHRASING?

steps: Quoting uses exact words in quotation marks; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.
So quoting is word-for-word; paraphrasing is in your own words.
solution.answer: Quoting uses exact words; paraphrasing restates the idea in your own words.

items.prompt: Why avoid OVERRELIANCE on one source?

steps: Leaning on one source makes the work narrow and possibly biased.
So using several sources gives a broader, more balanced, more reliable basis.
solution.answer: Several sources give a broader, more balanced, more reliable basis.

items.prompt: What does assessing a source's STRENGTHS AND LIMITATIONS mean?

steps: It means judging what a source does well and where it falls short for your task.
So it means weighing both its usefulness and its weaknesses.
solution.answer: Weighing both what a source offers and where it falls short for your task.
